subject.name: Mathematics
subject.description: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (Extended). Sample content: the questions below are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: Number
topics.summary: Types of number, fractions, decimals and percentages, standard form, bounds, ratio and proportion, compound interest.

topics.title: Algebra and graphs
topics.summary: Algebraic manipulation, equations and inequalities, sequences, functions, graphs and differentiation.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
topics.summary: Gradients, midpoints, lengths of line segments and equations of straight lines.

topics.title: Geometry
topics.summary: Angle properties, similarity, symmetry and circle theorems.

topics.title: Mensuration
topics.summary: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume, arcs and sectors.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Pythagoras' theorem, right-angled trigonometry, sine and cosine rules, 3D problems.

topics.title: Transformations and vectors
topics.summary: Reflections, rotations, translations, enlargements and vector geometry.

topics.title: Probability
topics.summary: Probability of single and combined events, tree diagrams, conditional probability.

topics.title: Statistics
topics.summary: Averages and range, grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms.

questions.stem: Amira invests $2500 in a savings account paying compound interest at a rate of 3.2% per year.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of the investment at the end of 4 years. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates used the multiplier 1.032 correctly. A common error was to calculate simple interest (2500 × 0.032 × 4) and add it to the principal, giving 2820.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the smallest whole number of years after which the investment will first be worth more than $3000.

markingPoints.text: M1 for a trial such as 2500 × 1.032^n with n = 5 or 6, or a correct logarithmic method

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who showed their trials clearly usually earned the method mark even when they misread their calculator display. Some stopped at 5 years without checking the value exceeded $3000.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write 0.000 047 3 in standard form.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Errors included 47.3 × 10^-6, which is not in standard form, and sign errors in the power.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The length of a rod is 12.4 cm, correct to the nearest millimetre. Write down the lower bound of the length.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave 12.3 or 12.45. Remember the bounds are half a unit of accuracy either side of the stated value.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 5(x − 3) = 2x + 9.
parts.examinerComment: Generally well done. Weaker candidates expanded 5(x − 3) as 5x − 3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Factorise completely 6x² − 15xy.

markingPoints.text: or B1 for a correct partial factorisation such as 3(2x² − 5xy) or x(6x − 15y)

parts.examinerComment: The word 'completely' signals that all common factors must be taken out. Many candidates removed only 3 or only x.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the nth term of the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, …

markingPoints.text: or B1 for 4n + k (k ≠ 3) or jn + 3 (j ≠ 0)

parts.examinerComment: Common errors were n + 4 and 4n + 7, the latter from using the first term as the constant.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt:
Solve the simultaneous equations. Show all your working.
3x + 2y = 16
 x − 2y = 0

markingPoints.text: M1 for adding the equations to eliminate y (4x = 16) or a correct substitution

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who showed the elimination step clearly were most successful. Answers without working could only gain the accuracy marks if both values were correct.

questions.stem: A is the point (2, 5) and B is the point (8, −3).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line AB.
parts.examinerComment: A frequent error was inverting the fraction (change in x over change in y). Sign errors were also common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the length of AB.

markingPoints.text: M1 for square root of their sum

parts.examinerComment: Well answered by most. Some candidates added the coordinates instead of subtracting.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of AB. Give your answer in the form (x, y).

markingPoints.text: or B1 for one correct coordinate

parts.examinerComment: Very well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. Find the number of sides of the polygon.
parts.examinerComment: Using the exterior angle is the most efficient method. Candidates using (n − 2) × 180 = 156n often made algebraic slips.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle AOC = 128°. Find angle ABC, where B is on the major arc. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for reason: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference

parts.examinerComment: Reasons must use correct geometrical language. 'Angle at centre is double' without reference to the circumference did not earn the mark.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Two similar bottles have heights 12 cm and 18 cm. The smaller bottle holds 400 ml. Calculate the volume the larger bottle holds, in ml.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates used the linear or area scale factor instead of cubing the length ratio for volume.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius 9 cm and angle 40°. Calculate the arc length, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates calculated the sector area instead of the arc length.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A solid cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Calculate its total surface area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: The most common error was to include only one circular end.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A cone has volume 300 cm³ and base radius 6 cm. Calculate the height of the cone, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who forgot the 1/3 obtained 2.65.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PQ = 7 cm and QR = 11 cm. Calculate angle QPR, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Labelling the opposite and adjacent sides on a sketch helped candidates choose the correct ratio.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 13 cm and angle BAC = 60°. Calculate the length of BC, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: A common error was evaluating (8² + 13² − 2 × 8 × 13) × cos 60, which shows a misunderstanding of the order of operations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the area of triangle ABC in part (b), in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle T with vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 2) onto triangle U with vertices (−1, 1), (−1, 3), (−2, 1).
parts.examinerComment: Candidates must give a single transformation. Combinations of transformations scored zero. Many omitted the centre of rotation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: a = (3, −2) and b = (−1, 4) written as column vectors. Find |2a + b|, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found 2a + b correctly. Some then gave the vector rather than its magnitude.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that both counters are red. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates treated the selection as with replacement and gave 25/64.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the two counters are different colours. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who drew a tree diagram were more likely to consider both orders.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that at least one counter is red, find the probability that both are red. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Conditional probability remains challenging. The condition reduces the sample space, so the denominator is P(at least one red).

questions.stem:
The masses, m kg, of 40 parcels are recorded.
0 < m ≤ 2: 6 parcels
2 < m ≤ 4: 14 parcels
4 < m ≤ 8: 12 parcels
8 < m ≤ 12: 8 parcels

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate an estimate of the mean mass, in kg.
parts.examinerComment: Common errors included using class widths or upper bounds instead of midpoints, and dividing by 4 (the number of classes).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On a histogram, find the frequency density for the class 4 < m ≤ 8.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. Some candidates divided by the upper class boundary.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Write down the modal class.
parts.examinerComment: With unequal class widths the modal class is the one with the highest frequency density. Here 2 < m ≤ 4 has density 7, the highest.
